title: ArtifactManifest — a pure function of sealed content
description: The canonical physical manifest. `artifact_id` IS the SHA-256 of these bytes canonicalized under artifact@1, which is only sound because the document is content-pure: it carries no build timestamp, builder identity, attempt id or hostname. Those live in the catalog row and the attempt row. Purity is what makes a byte-identical rebuild converge on one catalog row by rule instead of colliding. The L2 copy of this document is the ONLY reader input: the PostgreSQL JSONB projection is audit metadata and never opens an artifact.

format_version.description: The envelope format, mirrored from the plan so a reader can decide compatibility from the manifest alone without fetching the plan.

engines.description: Which engine produced which part, at which exact revision. Sorted by role so the encoding is stable.

components.description: Every physical file, hashed. The contract is that every byte is LISTED and VERIFIABLE -- not that an engine emits deterministic bytes, which is not promised and must not be assumed. Paths are normalized relative paths; absolute paths, '..', drive prefixes, symlinks, alternate data streams and duplicate normalized names are refused before any allocation.

required.description: A reader must refuse the artifact if a required component is missing; an optional one may be absent when a feature bit says so.

range_map.description: Optional reference to the block map, itself listed in components and hashed like any other file. Reserved in v1; whole-artifact hydration is the v1 serving path.

counts.description: Checked against configured allocation limits BEFORE memory is reserved. An untrusted count is an allocation instruction unless it is bounded first.

reader.description: The supported reader range this artifact declares. Startup and every binding change reject an unsupported artifact BEFORE traffic is switched to it.

required_features.description: Sorted, deduplicated. A reader that does not recognise one refuses; unknown OPTIONAL features are ignored.

probes.description: Deterministic verification queries run at seal and again after hydration. A probe is what turns 'the hashes matched' into 'the index answers', which is a different claim: a correctly transferred but wrongly built index passes checksums.

$comment: Fields deliberately ABSENT and which a validator must reject as additionalProperties: built_at, builder, builder_version, attempt_id, hostname, node_id, tenant_id, index_version_id. The first six are non-content metadata and belong to the catalog and attempt rows. The last two are authority, not content: an identical corpus in two tenants legitimately produces one artifact_id, and runtime authority uses ArtifactCacheKey { isolation_domain, logical_version_id, artifact_id } while durable keys carry tenant_id and index_version_id. Putting either in the manifest would make the content hash pretend to be an authorization boundary.
